verses.text: The Israelites broke faith over what had been set apart for the LORD. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of it. So the LORD's anger burned against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, near Beth Aven, east of Bethel. He told them to go up and scout the land, so they went and looked over Ai.
They came back and told Joshua, “You don't need to send everybody up. Two or three thousand men can attack Ai. There's no need to wear everyone out when there are so few people there.”
About three thousand men went up, but they ran from the men of Ai.
The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them. They chased them from the city gate as far as Shebarim and struck them down on the slope. The people's courage melted like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown before the LORD's ark. He and the elders of Israel stayed there until evening and put dust on their heads.

Joshua said, “Oh, Lord GOD, why did you bring these people across the Jordan at all, just to hand us over to the Amorites to be wiped out? If only we'd been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
Lord, what can I say now that Israel has turned and run from its enemies?
The Canaanites and everyone else in the land will hear about this, surround us, and erase our name from the earth. Then what will you do for your great name?”
The LORD told Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying there facedown?
Israel has sinned. They broke the covenant I commanded them to keep. They took things that had been set apart. They stole, they lied, and they even hid those things among their own belongings.

That's why the Israelites can't stand against their enemies. They turn and run because they themselves are now set apart for destruction. I won't be with you anymore unless you destroy what was set apart and is still among you.

Get up and set the people apart. Tell them, ‘Get yourselves ready for tomorrow. The LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Israel, something set apart for destruction is among you. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove it.”

In the morning come forward by tribe. The tribe the LORD singles out must come forward by clan. The clan he singles out must come forward by household. The household he singles out must come forward man by man.
Whoever is caught with what was set apart will be burned with everything he has, because he broke the LORD's covenant and did something disgraceful in Israel.’”
Joshua got up early the next morning and called Israel forward by tribe. The tribe of Judah was singled out.
He called Judah's clans forward, and the clan of Zerah was singled out. He called that clan forward man by man, and Zabdi was singled out.
He called Zabdi's household forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was singled out.
Joshua told Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and confess to him. Tell me what you did. Don't hide it from me.”
Achan answered, “I really did sin against the LORD, the God of Israel. Here's what I did.

I saw a beautiful Babylonian robe among the plunder, along with two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels. I wanted them, so I took them. They're buried in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver underneath.”
Joshua sent messengers who ran to the tent. Sure enough, the objects were hidden there with the silver underneath.
They took everything from the middle of the tent and brought it to Joshua and all the Israelites. They laid it out before the LORD.

Joshua and all Israel took Achan, a descendant of Zerah, and the silver, the robe, the wedge of gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, donkeys, sheep, tent, and everything he had to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, “Why have you brought trouble on us? Today the LORD will bring trouble on you.” All Israel stoned him. They burned them and threw stones on them.
They piled up a great heap of stones over Achan, and it's still there today. The LORD turned away from his fierce anger. That's why that place is still called the Valley of Achor.
